spec_match.rationale: Covers the full overflow-x × overflow-y value space with the spec's own vocabulary: scrollable vs non-scrollable values, the visible→auto coercion, the (removed) clip→hidden coercion, and the not-a/single-axis/dual-axis scroll container classification from §3.

interactive.rationale: Two selects drive the live stage via the longhands, the computed table refreshes from getComputedStyle on every change, and the per-axis script probe genuinely nudges scrollLeft/scrollTop and reports what moved.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The blurb promises a picker, live stage, specified→computed table, coercion flags, and classification; all five are present and real.

edge_cases.rationale: The edge-case list walks scroll×clip, scroll×visible, clip×visible, hidden×clip, and clip×clip — including the combinations whose behavior did NOT change, which is where wrong mental models come from.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus.com/feature/5067363861004288, the spec section, and the csswg change PR.

conformance.rationale: Every note the matrix can emit corresponds to a suite assertion (clip preserved, visible→auto unchanged, clip-visible preserved, clip-clip unscrollable, hidden script-scrollable); observed 5 pass / 3 fail split on Chromium 141 matches the matrix's own readouts.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 with autorun: scroll×clip computed to scroll/hidden with the rose 'legacy, pre-152' note, both axes moved under the script probe, and the classification honestly reported dual-axis; console clean. The preserved-clip branch requires a 152+ browser.

telemetry_health.rationale: sasc-matrix-clip-preserved only fires when detection reports support and the computed values kept clip; coerced browsers emit the separate sasc-matrix-legacy-fallback id with the observed values.

design_system.rationale: Selects are ivory-on-black-border with 44px min-height, coercion notes use accent-rose/emerald on paper (AA), classification emphasis uses accent-blue on stone; no raw hex anywhere.

accessibility.rationale: Native labelled selects with visible focus outlines, native buttons, the classification line is role=status aria-live=polite so probe outcomes are announced, and the stage is a keyboard-focusable labelled group.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Verified at 360×740 DPR3 and 1280×1600: panels stack under 720px, the five-column readout table scrolls in its own overflow-x container, no page-level horizontal overflow on either class; console clean apart from the environmental fonts.googleapis failure.

openQuestions.title: Add a copyable declaration + expected-vs-actual diff once a supporting browser is available
openQuestions.detail: On Chrome 152+, verify the emerald 'clip preserved — single-axis (new)' note and the y-axis 'refused (0)' probe result for scroll×clip, and consider emitting a spec-derived expected-computed column so the matrix can flag any future browser deviation explicitly.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive two panel grid selects control layout without horizontal overflow
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use minmax(0,1fr) tracks, stack panels on narrow viewports, give wide tables their own scroll container.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Matrix layout uses minmax(0,1fr) columns collapsing at 720px and the readout table lives in an overflow-x:auto wrapper; measured scrollWidth equals innerWidth at 360px and 1280px.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible select controls labelled pair live result
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use native selects with programmatically associated labels and announce results via a polite live region rather than visual change alone.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Both selects are label-wrapped native elements with 44px minimum height and focus-visible outlines; the classification/probe outcome is a role=status aria-live=polite region.

summary: The reference tool for the whole value space: pick any of the 25 pairs and get the browser's real computed values, the spec rule that fired, the scroll-container classification, and a script probe that proves it. On sandbox Chromium 141 it correctly shows the legacy clip→hidden coercion and dual-axis classification without simulating the new behavior.
